summary: Retest of the iteration_13 fixes. BACKEND: 15/15 new tests pass in test_iter14_sandbox.py, the 11 iter13 tests pass after updating two stale helpers, and the 16 iter12 tests pass. SANDBOX: two probe projects ran as different unprivileged uids (25674 and 26677), with gid equal to uid and no supplementary groups. Each probe got PermissionError on /app/backend/.env, /tmp/donas_previews/.mongo_admin, /tmp/donas_previews/_mongo and /proc/1/environ. mongodb://localhost:27017 is blocked by the guard. A probe can write to its own DB, and list_database_names returns only its own preview_{pid}. It cannot list or read the other project's work dir. It cannot use the other project's DB with its own credentials (not authorized), with guessed credentials (AuthenticationFailed) or without auth (requires authentication). ENV RESTART: after PUT /env, /preview/run returns installing, and the backend then sees NEW_VAR. PUBLIC: status/run return only {status, token}. A private project returns 404. The 21st call returns 429 even with a spoofed leftmost X-Forwarded-For. The public proxy works. STOP/DELETE: stop takes about 0.33s and leaves status 'stopped'. Stop and delete both remove the work dir, the preview DB and the p_{pid} mongo user. WORKSPACE UI regression: all pass ('Back-end rodando', the iframe shows the real /api/ping response, Reiniciar goes through installing back to running, the /sobre route works, the mobile toggle sets the iframe to about 266px, the versions sheet and share popover with public URL and QR open). LIVE PREVIEW RELOAD FAILS IN THE PREVIEW BUILD. When a visitor opens /p/{id}/live on a stopped backend, the backend starts, but the page keeps showing the 503 (empty #msg) and never sends a status poll. Cause: StrictMode runs the effect twice, so two POST /run calls go out at once. The second hits the busy ensure() lock and gets {status:'stopped'}, so it never starts polling. The first response, which said installing, belongs to the cancelled effect. When I delayed the second POST by 2s, polling started and the iframe remounted automatically, showing 'pong do backend UI' about 9s later. So the frameKey bump works and only the race is broken. KNOWN LIMITATION (high impact): the Python guard is bypassed by `python -S` or a subprocess with a cleared env (connect_ex 27017 returns 0) and by bash /dev/tcp. Through `python -S` with pymongo, a preview listed the platform mongod DBs ['admin','config','local','selfhost_test','test_database'], so full platform DB access is possible.

critical.issue: When the per-project lock is busy (another ensure is still in _scan/sync_files before RUNNERS[pid] is set), it returns status(pid), which is {status:'stopped'}. Clients treat this as final, so concurrent callers never poll. This is what breaks Live Preview auto-reload.

minor.issue: The guard is Python-level only. subprocess `python -S` (pymongo via sys.path) and bash /dev/tcp reach 127.0.0.1:27017. The platform mongod has no auth, so user code can read and write test_database (users, projects, env_enc). It can also reach 127.0.0.1:8001 and the 0.0.0.0:8010 plugins agent server. Mitigation without iptables: enable --auth on the platform mongod and use a credentialed MONGO_URL (the strongest fix available here), or run previews in a separate pod or container.

uid = 20000 + sha256(pid) % 40000. There is about a 50% chance of a collision by about 236 projects. Two projects that share a uid can read each other's /tmp/donas_previews/<pid> (source and .env vars). Allocate unique uids (a counter stored in the DB) or check for a collision before launch.

Preview uids can read /app source, /app/memory/test_credentials.md and /etc/supervisor/conf.d/supervisord_code_server.conf (which has the code-server PASSWORD). These files exist only in the preview env, but chmod o-r them or exclude them.
stop() deletes the whole work dir including .venv, so every stop or idle reap means a fresh pip install (about 10-60s) on the next visit. Consider keeping .venv and dropping only the source files.

ui_bugs.issue: No auto-reload after the backend starts when the backend was stopped. The run response of the effect that is still alive is {status:'stopped'} (lock race under StrictMode's double effect), so poll() is never scheduled. Fix both sides: (a) in ensure(), return {status:'starting'} when the lock is busy. (b) in LivePreview, keep polling when status is 'stopped' or null for a few tries, and ignore handle() results once alive is false.

action_items: Fix the ensure() busy-lock response: return {status:'starting'} instead of status(pid) when RUNNERS has no entry yet, or when the lock is held.
LivePreview.jsx: keep polling while status is not running, error or no_backend (with a cap), and guard handle() with alive so a cancelled effect's response is ignored.
Strongly recommended: enable auth on the platform mongod, because the python -S and bash /dev/tcp guard bypasses give full platform DB access.
Optional: chmod o-r sensitive non-.env files (memory/test_credentials.md, supervisor code_server conf), and keep .venv on stop.
critical_code_review_comments: runner.ensure: lock.acquire(blocking=False) followed by return status(pid) leaks a transient 'stopped' to callers. This is the root cause of the Live Preview failure.
runner._uid hash-mod uid allocation can collide, and the isolation model then fails silently.
GUARD_CODE patches only socket.socket.connect and connect_ex in CPython. Child processes started with -S, -I or a cleared PYTHONPATH, and non-Python tools, skip it.
LivePreview.jsx calls handle() after the effect is cancelled (no alive check), so a cancelled effect can still mutate the refs.

Live Preview repro: python iter13_ui_setup.py create, then preview/run, wait for running, then POST preview/stop, then open /p/{pid}/live and capture the POST /run responses (one is {status:'stopped'}) and count /status polls (currently 0). Root cannot readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd of preview processes, so match on args. runner_check.preview_dbs() needs /tmp/donas_previews/.mongo_admin (root).
rca of the issue: Live Preview no reload. Repro: stop the backend of a public project, then open /p/{id}/live. Under React.StrictMode the effect mounts, unmounts and mounts again, so there are two POST /run calls about 0ms apart. POST#1 takes the ensure() lock and is busy in _scan/sync_files before RUNNERS[pid] exists. POST#2 fails lock.acquire(blocking=False) and returns status(pid), which is {status:'stopped'}. The live effect (#2) sees 'stopped' and schedules no poll. Effect #1 got 'installing', but its alive flag is false. Result: zero status polls, and the iframe keeps the 503 build forever. Verified: when the second POST was delayed by 2s, polling started and the frame remounted with the real backend response 9s later. Mitigation: return 'starting' on lock contention and/or poll on 'stopped'. In a production build there is no double effect, but two visitors opening the page at the same time can still hit the race.
